author: Platform Documentation
deck: The platform can turn written content into a real, downloadable PDF — free and instant, no AI model involved. Here's what that actually looks like today, honestly, including what it can't do yet.
description: How PDF generation works on this platform: a deterministic, zero-cost template render, what it can produce today, and the two platform-side gaps that currently limit it to a single page of styled text.

image.alt: Abstract illustration of layered document pages in the platform's blue, teal, and gold palette, representing written content turned into a downloadable PDF.

public.body: Everything on this platform lives as a web page by default. But sometimes what you actually want is a document — something a reader can download, save, print, or forward without opening a browser. The platform can produce that: a real PDF, generated from the same written content, through the same governed object system as everything else.
public.title: Content doesn't have to stay on the page

public.body: A PDF here is built from a template — a layout with named fields — plus the data that fills those fields in. Nothing about turning text into a laid-out page requires a model to run: it's a direct, mechanical render, the same "already known, so a rule can do it" principle covered in the platform's article on what needs AI and what doesn't. That means generating a PDF costs nothing and returns in seconds, the same whether it's generated once or a hundred times.
public.title: How it actually works

public.body: Right now, a generated PDF is a single page of styled text — but styled meaningfully: real color, real hierarchy, sized headings, the platform's own palette rather than plain black-on-white. That's enough for a field guide, a one-page summary, a printable reference sheet. It is not yet able to lay out multiple pages, embed a diagram, or place a photograph inside the document — two separate, known gaps on the generation side mean those don't work yet, not a limit of what a PDF template is capable of in general.
public.title: What it can do today, honestly

public.body: Both gaps described above were traced to their exact cause today, not guessed at: the renderer's plugin set only ever registered plain text, and a separate normalization step was silently discarding every page after the first regardless of how many were defined. Both turned out to be small, isolated fixes in the same file, verified by generating real PDFs — a five-page template rendering as five pages, not one; rectangle, line, image and table elements rendering alongside text on one page. The fix is written, tested, and delivered as a reviewable change. It has not been merged or deployed yet, so the platform's live behavior is unchanged as of this writing: still one page, still text only. This paragraph is the thing to update once it lands.
public.title: What Changed Today, Before It's Live

public.body: Rendered from this site's own on-brand pdfme template — colors pulled straight from the platform's palette — through the same artifact-job pipeline described above. Still a single page of styled text, matching exactly what the live renderer can do today.
public.title: Download This Article as a PDF

public.body: Nothing about how you'd ask for a PDF needs to change when multi-page layouts and embedded graphics become available — the request stays the same; only what comes back gets richer. Until then, a single well-designed page, in the site's own colors, is the honest ceiling, and it's still a real, working, free document — not a placeholder.
public.title: What changes once the gaps close
